text: The Skyview High School Boundary Public Hearing of the Fairfax County School Board is called at the order of 6.06 p.m. Mr. Moon has submitted a request to attend tonight's meeting remotely due to a personal conflict, as he has a family commitment that is located in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Chair Lady has performed an initial review of Mr. Moon's request, and having found it to be in compliance with the school board's remote participation resolution, she has approved the request. Mr. Moon, please check your audio and video. Looks fine to me. Thank you.

I now ask board members who are physically present to vote on the following. All those in favor of confirming the chair's approval for Mr. Moon's request opposed? Okay, in favor? Mr. Frisch, Ms. Anderson, Ms. Marin, Ms. N. Joss Cumming-Cunning, Ms. Lady, and Dr. Anderson and myself.
Dr. Anderson did not. Okay. So we have how many? Okay, who's opposed? Dr. Anderson, abstain. Clerk, please announce the vote.

It's 6-1. Mr. Moon's participation is confirmed. Thank you. Good evening and welcome to the public hearing of the Skyview High School Boundaries. On behalf of the entire school board, I would like to thank you for sharing your comment with us. The hearing is being broadcast on Channel 99 and live streamed on YouTube and our website at www.fcps.edu forward slash live stream.

At the July 9th, 2026 regular meeting, Dr. Reid presented on Skyview High School Western Pyramid Superintendents Preliminary Boundary Recommendation. Tonight's public hearing is an opportunity for the public to provide comments on the approved boundary.

We have 45 pre-registered and walk-in speakers who will address the board at this public hearing. Speakers are allotted two minutes and we ask you to stay within the time limit. The timer will start when you begin to speak, and the timer will sound after two minutes.

Please ensure that your remarks are limited to the Skyview High School Western Pyramid Superintendent's preliminary boundary recommendation and that your remarks adhere to the school board's expectation for community participation. Included in those expectations are that only one person is allowed at the podium when speaking.

Neither adults or children may accompany a speaker at the podium. Copies of all expectations are available at the back of the auditorium. To assist with the flows of tonight's hearing, please ensure you are following along with the speakers list and are ready to go along as soon as your name is called.

If you have a hard copy of your testimony, please give it to the clerk. If you are virtual, please turn on your camera or when you are next in the line to speak so that you just have to unmute when you are called to speak. If you have electronic copies of your testimony and would like to share it with the board, Please email it to communityparticipation at fcps.edu.

When your name is called, the clerk will call your name two times before moving on to the next individual on the list. You may find copies of the speaker or speaking order in the back of the room or the board docs. Madam Deputy Clerk, please call our first speaker.

Gracia Rutser. My name is Gracia Rutser. I live in Fox Mill Estate, which is recommended to be rezoned from South Lakes to Skyview High School. As a rising 8th grader, I would be the first class to be zoned, and I am advocating for an opt-in model.

I've been excited to be a high school student since I was little. The choice of classes, being at a large school and dressing up as part of the hype squad, the chance to experience all of that is in jeopardy for middle school students slated to be rezoned. It causes me stress not to know what options there will be for students. I play the violin. At what point will there be a full orchestra?

Skyview has been highly promoted for its tech pathways, but what about the kids who aren't interested in those paths? For me, it is stressful thinking about trying to navigate a new school that is creating cultures versus one who has them up and running. Athletics will likely be introduced in my freshman year. What sports will Skyview have enough students for and when?

When will an actual stadium be built to house a varsity football team, cheerleaders, dance team, and a marching band? Will there be enough girls for flag football? None of us know the answers to these and many more questions. Let's talk homecoming, the time when both the pyramid and community come together.

I have marched in parades, had spirits days, even in elementary school, and watched my neighbors get dressed up for the dance. Homecoming is about recognizing alumni, Skyview is none. Skyview students will not get this experience for at least a few years. I want the opportunity to have upperclassmen to learn from who help set the tone, who model leadership.

I am worried about establishing a social group. It is said at the boundary meetings that kids are coming to Skyview from all over the county. When the new friend I meet lives across the county, what does that look like for having friends to hang out with in person. What school game do I go to on a Friday night? For some schools you have to have student ID from that school to attend. Where does that leave me as a Skyview student? So I asked this board to vote for Skyview to be an opt-in option until such a time that Skyview has full classes of 9th through 12th grade and the academic and extracurricular options are
known. I get to do and experience high school once in my life. Alakshi Nanagotil. Alakshi Nanagotil.

My daughter is a rising 11th grader at Westfield High School. I also have two younger sons who will one day attend Westfield. For example, my daughter is hoping to take AP Psychology or AP European History her senior year. The current boundary proposal puts Westfield at 72% capacity. FCPS's target is at least 80% utilization to be optimal. So please don't let the percentage dip lower than 72%. And if there's a way for us to get closer to 80, that would be even better.

One of the strongest programs at Westfield is our American Sign Language program.

We currently have two ASL teachers and we offer ASL levels one through four. If we could establish an ASL Academy program at Westfield, we could retain the strength of that program even in a smaller student body.
